extracted.intended_audience: Members of Parliament, ministers, and the politically engaged public concerned with East India Company governance
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and normative principles for how ministers and Parliament should examine, verify, and dispose of claims on colonial (Carnatic) revenues and how government should treat devastated colonial populations. Focuses on scrutiny of creditor claims, fiscal prudence, conflict-of-interest avoidance, and relief/recovery policy for an impoverished territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the burden of the proof on those who make the demand: 'The person who admits your debt stands excepted to as evidence; ... You say, you have a demand of some millions on the Indian Treasury; prove that you have acted by lawful authority; prove, at least, that your money has been bonâ fide advanced.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creditors seeking payment from the public treasury must demonstrate lawful authority and that funds were actually and bona fide advanced; ministers should require such proof before granting protection or payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry into authenticity, amount, and proprietors before payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Require inquiry into the authenticity of the demand, the actual amount of the claim, and identification of the real proprietors before any order of payment: ministers ordered payment 'without any sort of inquiry into its authenticity,--without a single step taken to settle even the amount of the demand,--without an attempt so much as to ascertain the real persons claiming a sum.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before disbursing public funds, authorities must ascertain who the claimants are, the legitimate amounts owed, and whether claims are genuine, with lists of proprietors produced and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid indiscriminate establishment of mixed valid and fraudulent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not establish all claims indiscriminately when valid and fraudulent claims are blended; the minister's approach of 'indiscriminately to establish them all' is criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims include both valid and suspect elements, the proper course is discrimination and investigation, not blanket establishment which risks rewarding fraud and confounding honest creditors with fraudulent ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require conferral beyond claimants' agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers must not act on representations from only the agents of the pretended creditors: 'through the course of the whole business he has never conferred with any but the agents of the pretended creditors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be informed by consultation with independent parties (e.g., the Court of Directors, local officials, and the alleged debtors) rather than solely the claimants' agents to avoid collusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in adjudicative forums
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts or tribunals hearing proof of claims must be impartial and not composed of creditors themselves: the Mayor's Court was said to be unfit because 'the members of that court were themselves creditors, and therefore could not sit as judges.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept as evidence only adjudications from impartial, independent tribunals; where judges or members have financial stakes, their findings should be treated with skepticism and not accepted without additional scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to statutory inquiry procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministers should comply with the inquiry steps prescribed by statute or act before authorizing payments: 'have not been satisfied with authorizing the payment of this demand without such inquiry as the act has prescribed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When law prescribes inquiry procedures, executive action must follow them; bypassing prescribed investigations undermines accountability and invites fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require access to debtor records for detection of fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize inspection of the debtor's (e.g., Nabob's) exchequer and records to detect collusion: 'The ministers never authorized any person to enter into his exchequer and to search his records.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective fraud detection may require authorized auditors or investigators to examine local financial records; without that access, allegations of fraud cannot be probed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand transparent lists of proprietors/claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Insist on disclosure of the proprietors/claimants: 'no list has ever yet been laid before the Court of Directors,--of proprietors who are known to be in a collusive shuffle.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require submission of detailed, stable claimant lists and resist arrangements where proprietorship deliberately shuffles to obscure real beneficiaries; transparency prevents collusion and arbitrary distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid compounding unpaid interest into new capital without verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not add arrears of interest to create a new enlarged capital without proof that money was actually advanced: ministers 'added the arrear of twelve per cent interest ... to make a new capital' and 'has again grafted on this meliorated stock a perpetual annuity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before capitalizing interest or creating perpetual annuities, verify underlying advances and legal entitlement; avoid mechanically transforming accumulated interest into higher principal that burdens public revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept late private court 'proof' as sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Be skeptical of creditor proofs produced belatedly in private/local courts (e.g., Mayor's Court) especially when earlier records and public inquiries contradict them: 'But it seems the right honorable gentleman's favorite soucar cavalry have proved the payment before the Mayor's Court at Madras! Have they so? Why, then, defraud our anxiety and their characters of that proof?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the context, timing, and impartiality of local proofs; late or self-interested affidavits should not supplant long-standing public records or require ad hoc trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize genuine local (native) creditors and relief for the population
rubrics_metrics.description: Give priority to native bonâ fide creditors and to the relief of a devastated population over rewarding foreign speculators: 'the creditors most certainly not fraudulent are the natives ... they lent bonâ fide' and the people must be maintained to enable recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public revenues are scarce, distribution should favor those demonstrably entitled through honest dealings and the needs of the population; policy should support rebuilding (expense/investment), not immediate extraction for creditor payouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test credibility by consistency of motives and statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use coherence and consistency as indicators of honesty: 'It is one of the known indications of guilt to stagger and prevaricate in a story, and to vary in the motives that are assigned to conduct.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess officials' and claimants' credibility by whether their justifications and motives are consistent across documents and statements; shifting rationales suggest unfair dealing or collusion and warrant deeper investigation.
